title: Lane-aware hybrid dequant pass with KV-cache window hints and microbatch coalescing
author: Evan Park
description: Motivation: reduce token-cost and tail-latency for quantized INT8/FP8 inference by fusing a lane-aware hybrid dequantization pass that opportunistically keeps some heads in low-precision while dequantizing others, combined with KV-cache window hinting to avoid unnecessary KV prefetch for short context reuse. This PR implements a new compiler pass (DequantLanePass) plus a small runtime hint protocol for KV windows and a microbatch coalescer that groups short-lived requests without increasing max latency. The goals were: 1) improve throughput on mixed-length workloads, 2) avoid per-token dequant overhead for heads that can safely remain quantized, 3) reduce redundant KV prefetch I/O when working sets are small. Summary of changes: added DequantLanePass with a lane-sampling heuristic and per-head scale-tracking; added runtime KV window hints and a conservative prefetch backoff; implemented a microbatch_coalescer that targets 1-3 ms additional latency budget for tiny requests and aggregates tokens to amortize dequant and kernel launch costs; updated quant kernels to expose a light-weight vectorized requant path used when lanes are partially dequantized. Includes new unit and integration tests and benchmark harness. Checklist: [x] design doc/rationale included, [x] unit tests, [x] integration perf test, [x] docs RFC, [x] canary rollout plan. Performance: internal bench on A100x8, mixed prompt distribution (90% short <128, 10% long 2k) showed token/sec +14% and p99 latency -8% compared to baseline dequant-all approach while maintaining output parity within eval tolerances. On smaller GPUs (T4 emulation) we see +9% throughput and slightly higher variance at p99 (+3%) which we mitigate via canary traffic shaping. Backwards compatibility: runtime hinting is optional and defaults to conservative behavior when older components are present. Rollout: staged canary on Dedicated us-west-2 with circuit-breaker to main model variants. See release_notes for user-facing impact.

review_comments: Asha Patel: Interesting approach. Two concerns: (1) how do we guarantee numeric parity when only a subset of heads are dequantized? Need a deterministic fallback if eval drifts. (2) microbatching could introduce head-of-line delay for single-token steady traffic. Please add metrics and a knob to bound latency.

Author (Evan Park): Added per-head scale tracking and a small 'reconcile' pass that forces full dequant on detected drift windows. Microbatch_coalescer has a max-wait knob and tracks per-route latency. See new tests and metrics in latest commit h8c13d4.

Liam O'Connor: KV hint API looks clean. Please ensure older coordinators ignore hints gracefully; and add a metric for hint utilization ratio. Also add a comment on why conservative backoff was chosen vs predictive prefetching.
Author (Evan Park): Older coordinators are handled: hint is optional and default false; added 'kv_hint_utilization' metric and documented the rationale in the RFC (latency vs memory tradeoff).
Zoe Martinez: Can we avoid touching public kernel registration surface? I worry about SDK compat. Also request small microbenchmark across T4/RTX profiles.
Author (Evan Park): Kernel surface changes are additive; vectorized requant path registers behind a feature flag. Microbenchmarks added under benchmarks/quant for T4 emulation.
ci_checks: benchmark-regression-check: warn (p99 variance +0.9% on small GPU), approved after reviewer signoff
release_notes: Added lane-aware hybrid dequant pass: reduces cost by keeping stable heads quantized and selectively dequantizing others; introduces optional KV-cache window hinting to avoid redundant prefetch; provides a microbatch coalescer to amortize dequant and kernel launch overhead for short requests. Default behavior is conservative and backward compatible. Can be enabled incrementally via runtime flags and canary policies.
rollback_plan: Disable feature-flag for vectorized requant and revert runtime kv_hint flag; circuit-breaker in canary routing will divert traffic to baseline model variant. Ops runbook updated at docs/runbooks/quant-rollback.md
benchmark_summary: A100x8 mixed workload: +14% throughput, p99 -8%; T4 emulation: +9% throughput, p99 +3% mitigated via traffic shaping. Small regression monitored in rare T4 cases; targeted knobs added.
notes: Non-breaking performance improvement. Follow-up work: (1) explore predictive KV prefetch using short-term locality model, (2) autotune lane sampling thresholds by route, (3) extend pass to FP8 per-layer heuristics.
